cards.name: Exposure
cards.summary: Photographic exposure change in f-stops, worked out in linear light, plus an Offset that shifts the black level and a Gamma Correction for midtones. Can act on the whole image (Master) or on the red, green and blue channels separately.
use_for: Rescue an under-exposed press photo or interview clip by +0.5 to +1 stop
White flash-frame hit on a cut or a beat in a trailer or reel (Exposure keyframed up and back down)
Darken a background plate by -1 stop so lower thirds and captions read on top
Fade to / from white between documentary chapters
Quick warm or cool cast with Individual Channels (Red Exposure up, Blue Exposure down)
avoid: Values above about +3 stops on a static shot: the frame clips to flat white and loses all detail
Pushing Offset: it lifts blacks into a milky grey that looks like a bad TV signal
Using it for contrast: it scales brightness, use Curves or Levels for contrast

params.name: Channels:
params.does: Master (one set of controls) or Individual Channels (separate R, G, B controls)

params.name: Exposure
params.does: Master exposure in f-stops (each +1 doubles brightness)
params.typical: -1 to +1.5 for correction; 3 to 5 for a flash hit

params.name: Offset
params.does: Adds a constant to every pixel in linear light: mainly lifts (+) or crushes (-) shadows and midtones, highlights barely move

params.name: Gamma Correction
params.does: Midtone gamma; above 1 brightens midtones, below 1 darkens

params.name: Red Exposure
params.does: Red channel exposure in stops (only with Channels: = 2)

params.name: Blue Exposure
params.does: Blue channel exposure in stops (only with Channels: = 2)
params.typical: -0.4 to -0.1 for a warm cast, positive for cool

params.name: Bypass Linear Light Conversion
params.does: Applies the maths to the raw pixel values instead of converting to linear light first

cards.scripting: Exposure is in stops: the harvested range is -100..100 but anything beyond about +/-5 is a solid white or black frame. The Red/Green/Blue Exposure, Offset and Gamma Correction properties only take effect when 'Channels:' = 2 (Individual Channels); set 'Channels:' before writing them. 'Bypass Linear Light Conversion' is a checkbox (0/1).

verified.note: +1.5 stops brightens the whole frame strongly (mean luma +55), the white wall and white clothing clip to white and shadows lift: a clear overexposed look.

cards.name: Gamma/Pedestal/Gain
cards.summary: Per-channel video-style colour controls: Gamma bends the midtones, Pedestal adds an offset to the black level, Gain multiplies the brightness of each of the red, green and blue channels. Black Stretch brightens the darkest values for all channels.
use_for: Quick warm (archival, nostalgia) or cool (night, tension) cast on a documentary clip
Lift the blacks slightly for a faded archival or flashback look
Match the colour balance of two cameras or two news feeds in a split-screen
Cool night / day-for-night shift on B-roll (Red and Green Gain down to about 0.8, Blue Gain about 1.1)
avoid: Large Gain on one channel: highlights clip into neon-coloured blotches
High Pedestal values: blacks turn into a flat grey haze
Heavy 4K grading: Lumetri Color is faster and gives more control

params.name: Black Stretch
params.does: Remaps the lowest pixel values; higher brightens the shadows of all channels

params.name: Red Gain
params.does: Multiplies the red channel (1 = unchanged)

params.name: Blue Gain
params.does: Multiplies the blue channel
params.typical: 0.75 to 0.95 for warmth, 1.1 to 1.2 for a cool look

params.name: Red Gamma
params.does: Red midtone gamma (1 = unchanged)

params.name: Blue Gamma
params.does: Blue midtone gamma

params.name: Blue Pedestal
params.does: Offset added to the blue black level

params.name: Red Pedestal
params.does: Offset added to the red black level

cards.scripting: Gamma and Gain default to 1 and Pedestal to 0, so the values are in normalised 0-1 pixel units; the harvested +/-32000 range is meaningless in practice. Keep Gamma 0.5-2, Gain 0.5-2, Pedestal -0.2..0.2. Black Stretch range is 1..4 (1 = no stretch). Render-verified: Red Gain 1.3 / Blue Gain 0.75 / Red Pedestal 0.04 gives a strong warm cast, so the 0-1 units hold.

verified.note: Strong warm orange-magenta cast: red up about 40 and blue down about 38 levels, with red lifted in the shadows from the Red Pedestal.

cards.name: Hue/Saturation
cards.summary: Rotates hue and changes saturation and lightness of the whole image (or a chosen colour range), and with Colorize tints the whole frame a single hue, like sepia or a brand-colour monotone.
use_for: Desaturate archival or flashback footage to black and white or a muted look
Colorize a background clip into a single brand colour (saffron, deep blue) behind headline text
Pull saturation down on a busy press shot so captions and graphics read
Sepia tint for historical sections of a documentary
Fast hue-flicker glitch on a reel beat (keyframed Master Hue)
avoid: Rotating Master Hue on footage with faces: skin goes green or purple
Master Lightness to brighten or darken: it flattens contrast, use Levels or Curves
Colorize Saturation above about 60: garish, cartoonish monotone

params.name: Channel Control
params.does: Which colour range the hue/sat/lightness sliders edit (popup)

params.name: Master Hue
params.does: Hue rotation in degrees
params.typical: -20 to 20 for subtle shifts; 180 for a complementary-colour glitch (not a true invert)

params.name: Master Saturation
params.does: Saturation change; -100 = black and white

params.name: Master Lightness
params.does: Lightens toward white or darkens toward black

params.name: Colorize
params.does: Checkbox: tint the whole image with one hue

params.name: Colorize Hue
params.does: Hue of the tint in degrees

params.name: Colorize Saturation
params.does: Strength of the tint colour

params.name: Colorize Lightness
params.does: Brightness of the tinted image

cards.scripting: Master Hue and Colorize Hue are angles in degrees (no harvested min/max). Colorize is a 0/1 checkbox and overrides the Master sliders when on. 'Channel Range' is a custom property and cannot be set. Editing a single colour range by script (Channel Control 2-7 then the sliders) is unverified: the harvest exposes only the Master Hue/Saturation/Lightness properties, so per-range values may not be reachable; use Lumetri Color or Change to Color for targeted colour shifts. Premiere: Color Balance (HLS) covers Master Hue/Saturation/Lightness; for Colorize use Tint or Lumetri Color.

verified.note: Colorize turns the whole frame into an orange-brown sepia monotone; stripes, dark clothing and flowers all collapse to one hue.

cards.name: Leave Color
cards.summary: Desaturates the whole image except pixels close to one chosen colour, giving a selective-colour (colour pop) look such as a red flag on a black-and-white frame.
use_for: Keep the party or flag colour (saffron, green, red) while the rest of a rally shot goes grey
Point the viewer at one object in an explainer (a red file, a marked map region)
Dramatic trailer or reel beat that drains colour except one accent
Emphasise a brand-colour prop in a news promo
avoid: Picking red or orange on shots with faces: skin tones fall inside the tolerance and stay patchy
Very low Tolerance on compressed footage: noisy speckled edges
Leaving Amount to Decolor at its default 0: the effect does nothing

params.name: Amount to Decolor
params.does: How much of the non-matching colour is removed (100 = full grey)

params.name: Color To Leave
params.does: The colour kept in full saturation
params.typical: the flag / prop colour, e.g. #C8102E red, #FF9933 saffron

params.name: Tolerance
params.does: How far from the chosen colour a pixel can be and still keep its colour

params.name: Edge Softness
params.does: Softens the boundary between kept and removed colour

params.name: Match colors
params.does: Compare by RGB values or by hue only (popup)
params.typical: 2 (Using Hue) for footage with varying light

cards.scripting: Default Amount to Decolor is 0, so always set it. 'Color To Leave' takes "#RRGGBB". Sample the real colour from the frame first: the effect is very sensitive to the exact hue. Match colors popup: 1 = Using RGB, 2 = Using Hue. Premiere 2026 has no Leave Color; its equivalent is Color Pass (Similarity, Reverse, Color).

verified.note: Selective colour: the greens, a blue block and the plants go grey while the red stripes, red foreground blocks and flowers keep their colour.

cards.name: Levels
cards.summary: Classic levels: remaps the input black point, white point and midtone gamma to new output black and white levels, for contrast, brightness and fades. The per-channel histogram edits live in a custom property, so by script only the RGB master controls are reachable.
use_for: Add contrast to a flat news or interview clip (raise Input Black, lower Input White)
Faded matte look for documentary flashbacks (raise Output Black)
Fade from or to black by keyframing Output White
Even out exposure between photos in a press-photo montage
avoid: Input Black above about 0.2: shadows crush to solid black and faces lose detail
Expecting per-channel colour edits by script: use Levels (Individual Controls)
Large Gamma moves on 8-bit footage: banding in skies and gradients

params.name: Input Black
params.does: Input level mapped to black (normalised 0-1)

params.name: Input White
params.does: Input level mapped to white (normalised 0-1)

params.name: Gamma
params.does: Midtone gamma (>1 brightens midtones)

params.name: Output Black
params.does: Darkest output level; raising it gives matte / faded blacks

params.name: Output White
params.does: Brightest output level; lowering it dims highlights

params.name: Channel:
params.does: Which channel the histogram shows and edits in the UI

cards.scripting: Values are normalised 0-1 (the UI shows 0-255 in an 8 bpc project; script 1.0 = 255). The Input/Output/Gamma properties edit the RGB master; per-channel values sit inside the custom 'Histogram' property and are not settable, so use 'Levels (Individual Controls)' for per-channel work. 'Clip To Output Black/White' popups (1 On, 2 Off, 3 Off for 32 bpc Color, the default) are left at default.

verified.note: Punchy contrast: luma spread rises from 48 to 72, blacks crush (dark clothing near black) and the white wall and white stripes clip to white.

cards.name: Levels (Individual Controls)
cards.summary: The same levels remap as Levels, but every channel (RGB master, Red, Green, Blue, Alpha) has its own exposed Input Black/White, Gamma and Output Black/White, so each can be set and keyframed separately.
use_for: Warm or cool grade by bending one channel's gamma (Red Gamma up, Blue Gamma down)
Blue-tinted shadows by lifting Blue Output Black; lift Green Output Black a little too for true teal (Blue alone plus a warm Red Gamma turns dark navy purple)
Contrast plus colour correction in one effect for interview clips
Tighten an alpha matte with Alpha Input Black/White on keyed footage
avoid: Large per-channel moves: skin tones turn orange or green
Input Black above about 0.2: crushes shadows
Forgetting it is normalised: 255-style values clamp to a white frame

params.name: Input Black
params.does: RGB master input black point (0-1)

params.name: Input White
params.does: RGB master input white point (0-1)

params.name: Gamma
params.does: RGB master midtone gamma

params.name: Red Gamma
params.does: Red channel midtone gamma

params.name: Blue Gamma
params.does: Blue channel midtone gamma

params.name: Blue Output Black
params.does: Lifts blue in the shadows

params.name: Output Black
params.does: RGB master output black (matte look)

params.name: Alpha Input White
params.does: Alpha level mapped to fully opaque (matte tightening)

cards.scripting: All values normalised 0-1. 'Channel:' only chooses which histogram the UI shows; every channel's properties are set directly by name (Red Gamma, Blue Output Black, ...). Clip To Output Black/White popups (1 On, 2 Off, 3 Off for 32 bpc Color, the default) left at default. Preferred over 'Levels' whenever a script needs per-channel control.

verified.note: Visible warm grade (red up, green and blue down) with slightly deeper blacks; the navy areas shift purple because Blue Output Black lifts only blue, not teal.

cards.name: Lumetri Color
cards.summary: Adobe's full grading panel inside one effect: white balance, exposure and tone, creative Looks/LUTs, fade and vibrance, curves, colour wheels, HSL secondary keying and a vignette. Gives everything from a clean correction to a stylised film grade.
use_for: One-stop correction of interview and B-roll clips (Temperature, Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows)
Consistent look across a documentary or explainer by putting it on an adjustment layer
Cinematic trailer grade: contrast, Faded Film, vignette
Desaturate background plates or flashbacks with Saturation
Warm up cold press-conference footage before compositing graphics on it
avoid: Values near the harvested extremes (Temperature/Tint +/-300, Contrast +/-150): far past the UI sliders and look broken
Stacking several Lumetri instances on every layer: slow; grade once on an adjustment layer
Relying on Look / Input LUT indices: the list depends on the LUTs installed on the machine

params.name: Temperature
params.does: White balance warm (+) / cool (-) (Basic Correction)

params.name: Exposure
params.does: Overall exposure in stops (Basic Correction)

params.name: Contrast
params.does: Basic Correction contrast

params.name: Highlights
params.does: Recovers (-) or brightens (+) the bright tones

params.name: Shadows
params.does: Opens (+) or deepens (-) the dark tones

params.name: Saturation
params.does: Basic Correction saturation, 100 = unchanged, 0 = B&W

params.name: Faded Film
params.does: Lifts and softens the blacks for a faded print look (Creative)

params.name: Amount
params.does: Vignette amount; negative darkens the edges

cards.scripting: Effect properties are flat and many display names repeat (Active x12, Input LUT x2, Intensity x2, Look x2, HDR White x2, Temperature/Tint/Contrast/Sharpen x2, Saturation x3). AE's lookup by name returns the FIRST: Temperature, Tint, Saturation, Exposure, Contrast = Basic Correction; Sharpen, Vibrance, Faded Film = Creative; Amount/Midpoint/Roundness/Feather = Vignette. The later copies (HSL Secondary 'Correction' sliders, Creative Look Intensity) are not reachable by name ('Name#2' passes the validator but ae_lib will not find it); address them by property index if ever needed. Curves, Color Wheels, Split Toning, HSL Sliders, Wheels are custom blobs and cannot be set: for those, apply a saved .ffx preset. Look and Input LUT popups index the installed LUT list (1 = None; order is machine-specific). The first 'Intensity' (0-100, default 50) in Basic Correction is unverified. Practical ranges are narrower than harvested: Temperature/Tint and tone sliders +/-100, Exposure +/-3, Vignette Amount +/-3, Saturation 0-200.

verified.note: Warm, saturated, higher-contrast grade with a clear dark vignette (corners about 50 levels darker); the first Temperature and Amount names do hit Basic Correction and Vignette.

cards.name: OCIO CDL Transform
cards.summary: Applies an ASC CDL grade (slope, offset, power, saturation) read from a .cdl, .cc or .ccc file through OpenColorIO, so a colourist's or DIT's grade can be reproduced exactly. Without a CDL file it does nothing.
use_for: Apply the on-set / DIT CDL delivered with camera footage so AE comps match the grade
Reuse a grade exported from DaVinci Resolve or Baselight as a CDL across a documentary series
Undo a CDL (Inverse transform) before compositing, then re-apply it on top
avoid: Using it without the matching CDL file: no visible change
Applying a CDL meant for log footage to Rec.709 footage: wrong contrast and colour

params.name: CCCID
params.does: Which correction inside a .ccc collection file to use (popup filled from the file)

params.name: Inverse transform
params.does: Checkbox: applies the inverse of the CDL

cards.scripting: Needs a CDL file chosen with the effect's File button (the 'File' group has no settable property in the harvest). CCCID popup had min = max = 1 when harvested (it is filled from the loaded file). Probably requires the project to use OCIO colour management (Project Settings > Color); unverified. For automation, set it up by hand and save an .ffx preset.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs an OCIO config / file chosen by hand), so no gallery frame was rendered.
verified.second_note: gallery/ae/index.json has no entry (needs_input cards are skipped by gallery.py), so no frame exists; needs_input is right because the CDL file is picked with a browse button no script can set and CCCID is filled from that file (harvest min = max = 1); card text matches Adobe's description (file browse, CCCID list, Inverse, Information).

cards.name: OCIO Color Space Transform
cards.summary: Converts pixels from one OpenColorIO colour space to another (for example camera log such as S-Log3 or LogC into ACEScg or Rec.709), using the project's OCIO config.
use_for: Convert log camera footage (S-Log3, V-Log, LogC) into Rec.709 or the working space before grading
Bring ACES / EXR 3D renders into the working space of the comp
Mix footage from different cameras in one colour-managed documentary timeline
avoid: Using it in a project that is not set up for OCIO: the colour-space menus are empty and nothing changes
Converting twice (once here and once by footage interpretation): double transform, washed-out or crushed image

params.name: Input Color Space
params.does: Colour space the layer is currently in (popup from the OCIO config)

params.name: Output Color Space
params.does: Colour space to convert to (popup from the OCIO config)

params.name: Reset Control
params.does: Resets the menus to the config defaults

cards.scripting: Both colour-space popups are built from the active OCIO config: in the harvest project they reported min = max = 1 with defaults 80 and 1371908864 (config IDs, not menu indices), so ae_lib's range clamp forces any scripted value to 1 and a script cannot reliably choose a colour space. Set the menus by hand and save an .ffx preset, or interpret the footage's colour space instead. Likely requires OCIO colour management in Project Settings (unverified). Premiere's equivalent is Color Space Transform (source / target colour space menus plus tone mapping).

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs an OCIO config / file chosen by hand), so no gallery frame was rendered.
verified.second_note: no frame exists (not in gallery index); both colour-space popups come from the project's OCIO config and were harvested with min = max = 1, so no scripted demo can pick a conversion; needs_input and empty demo_settings are correct.

cards.name: OCIO Display Transform
cards.summary: Applies an OpenColorIO display / view transform (for example ACES to sRGB or Rec.709 SDR video) to the layer, baking the look of the viewer into the pixels; Inverse brings display-referred images into scene-linear.
use_for: Bake the ACES / OCIO view transform into a render when delivering Rec.709 from a scene-linear comp
Inverse-transform logos, screenshots or graphics so they keep their colours inside an ACES comp
Check a scene-linear render on a specific display / view combination
avoid: Using it in a non-OCIO project: menus are empty and nothing happens
Applying it on top of a project that already applies the same view transform on output: double tone-mapping

params.name: Input Color Space
params.does: Colour space of the incoming pixels (OCIO config popup)

params.name: Display Device
params.does: Target display (OCIO config popup)

params.name: View Transform
params.does: View for that display (OCIO config popup)

params.name: Inverse transform
params.does: Checkbox: applies the inverse display transform
params.typical: 1 for graphics going into a linear comp

cards.scripting: Input Color Space, Display Device and View Transform popups come from the OCIO config and were harvested with min = max = 1, so scripts cannot choose them (values clamp to 1). Inverse transform and Reset Control are 0/1 checkboxes. Configure by hand and save an .ffx preset. Likely needs OCIO colour management in Project Settings (unverified).

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs an OCIO config / file chosen by hand), so no gallery frame was rendered.
verified.second_note: no frame exists (not in gallery index); Input / Display / View popups are filled from the OCIO config (harvest min = max = 1) and Inverse alone on an unconfigured transform proves nothing, so needs_input is correct; summary and params match Adobe's description.

cards.name: OCIO File Transform
cards.summary: Applies a LUT or colour-transform file (for example .cube, .3dl, .csp, .clf, .spi3d) through OpenColorIO. Without a chosen file it does nothing.
use_for: Apply a camera manufacturer's log-to-Rec.709 LUT to drone or cinema footage
Apply a show LUT or film-emulation LUT for a trailer or documentary look
Inverse a LUT to get back to log before compositing
avoid: Applying a log LUT to footage that is already Rec.709: harsh contrast and oversaturation
Expecting it to work without a file: no visible change

params.name: Inverse transform
params.does: Checkbox: applies the inverse of the file transform

cards.scripting: The LUT file is chosen with the effect's File button; the harvest shows no settable file property (the 'File' group is a header and the remaining properties are unnamed). A script can only toggle 'Inverse transform'. Configure by hand and save an .ffx preset, or use AE's Apply Color LUT / Lumetri Input LUT instead. May require OCIO colour management (unverified).

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs an OCIO config / file chosen by hand), so no gallery frame was rendered.
verified.second_note: no frame exists (not in gallery index); the LUT file is chosen with a browse button and only Inverse transform is settable, so a script cannot produce a visible demo; needs_input is correct.

cards.name: OCIO Look Transform
cards.summary: Applies a named 'look' defined in the OpenColorIO config (a show grade or creative LUT) between an input and an output colour space.
use_for: Apply a series-wide show look defined in the studio's OCIO config to every documentary episode
Preview a creative grade on CG renders inside an ACES pipeline
Remove a look (Inverse transform) to get back to the ungraded plate
avoid: Using it with an OCIO config that defines no looks: nothing to choose, no change
Wrong Input / Output colour spaces: the look lands on the wrong encoding and looks broken

params.name: Input Color Space
params.does: Colour space of the incoming pixels (OCIO config popup)

params.name: Look
params.does: Which look from the config to apply (popup)

params.name: Output Color Space
params.does: Colour space after the look (OCIO config popup)

params.name: Inverse transform
params.does: Checkbox: applies the inverse of the look

cards.scripting: Look and colour-space popups come from the OCIO config and were harvested with min = max = 1 (defaults 79 / 1 / 0 are config IDs), so a script cannot choose them (values clamp to 1). Needs an OCIO config that defines looks and probably OCIO colour management in Project Settings (unverified). Configure by hand and save an .ffx preset; Premiere's nearest is a Lumetri Color Creative Look.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs an OCIO config / file chosen by hand), so no gallery frame was rendered.
verified.second_note: no frame exists (not in gallery index); Look and colour-space popups come from the OCIO config (harvest min = max = 1), so needs_input with empty demo_settings is correct.
